activity.notes: This Activity represents Hannibal Barca's final securely attested Bithynian military-service phase. After leaving the Seleucid sphere and later reaching the court of Prusias of Bithynia, Hannibal supported Bithynia against Pergamon and is credited with a naval victory conventionally dated to 184 BCE. His death at Libyssa is usually placed around 183/182 BCE. ATLAS therefore records only c.184-c.183 BCE here, with approximate year bounds, rather than inventing a precise date for his arrival in Bithynia.

sources.title: Hannibal Barca
sources.citation_text: Livius places Hannibal with Prusias of Bithynia after his Armenian stay, records his naval victory over the Pergamene fleet in 184 BCE, and dates his death to winter 183/182 BCE.

sources.title: Eutropius, Short History, Book 4
sources.citation_text: Eutropius states that after Antiochus' defeat Hannibal fled to Prusias, king of Bithynia, and later died there when Roman surrender demands threatened him.
